summary_html: **CAPTA §5106a(c)** requires every state to maintain **Citizen Review Panels** that evaluate CPS policies. Project Milk Carton checks whether panels are active, independent, and publicly reporting.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: In a foster-care class action the court recognized that foster children hold a substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risk of harm and to reasonable safety, but held the jury was misinstructed by treating the professional-judgment standard of care as the right itself, and it narrowed the systemwide injunction.
key_cases.relevance: Demonstrates the role of independent external review, the function CAPTA assigns to citizen review panels.
key_cases.quote: We hold that foster children have a constitutional substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risks of harm and a right to reasonable safety.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a juvenile court's practice of sealing parents' ex parte motions for public funding of expert services violated GR 15 and article I, section 10 because no Ishikawa analysis was performed, and that applying GR 15's notice requirements in termination cases comports with due process.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the balance between parental privacy and public scrutiny that any external review of dependency practice must observe.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the superior court's ex parte sealing practice and the sealing of the disputed documents violate the court rules and Washington Constitution article I, section 10.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the discretionary right to counsel for children in RCW 13.34.100(7)(a) satisfies article I, section 3, and further held that the confidentiality of juvenile dependency records under RCW 13.50.100(2) survives appeal so appellate courts should seal such records on their own motion.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the statutory confidentiality limits any external review body must work within when examining dependency case files.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the confidential nature of dependency proceedings granted by RCW 13.50.100(2) is not lost through appeal
